purpose: Shows how far into the wage distribution the new minimum reached.
how: Counts the jobs at each hourly wage in 2018 and in 2020.
shows (written by make.py): The share of jobs paid below 12.50 falls from 25.0 percent to 2.6 percent.

purpose: Tests whether jobs were lost once the minimum rose, and how much wages and hours moved.
how: Compares Northvale's counties with their neighbours year by year, relative to the year before the raise.
shows (written by make.py): After the raise employment moves between -0.2 and 0.4 percent, while wages rise by 2.3 to 3.4 percent.

purpose: Asks whether places where the new minimum bit harder lost more jobs.
how: Bins 400 counties by the share of jobs paid below the new minimum and fits a line through all of them.
shows (written by make.py): The slope is 0.9, with a standard error of 1.3: no sign of more job loss where the bite was larger.

purpose: Looks for the industries where the raise cost jobs.
how: Estimates the effect of the raise separately in each industry.
shows (written by make.py): Only food service loses jobs, -1.9 percent.

purpose: Splits the wage gain into raises within firms and moves between them.
how: Decomposes the change in the mean wage into within-firm, between-firm and composition terms.
shows (written by make.py): Raises within firms make up 2.4 of the 3.4 percent gain.
